messages.subject: Area offset in spAbundance
parts:
Hi Jeff,

I have a multispecies (n = 3) dataset, with say 15 sampling sites and 2 sampling occasions. In each occasion I visited the sampling sites, I performed a transect of a different length (sampling was time-adjusted rather than space-limited). I thought I had to calculate an average of transect length per site, so that the offset would be a vector of length equal the  number of sites. However,  when I tried to run a N-mixture model with spNMix, I was returned an error indicating offset should have the same length as sample sites X occasions X species (15 X 2 X 3 = 90). Does that mean I can specify varying lengths per site? Also, how should I build this vector, site 1 X ocasion 1, site 1 X occasion 2, site 2 X occasion 2, and so on or all lengths on occasions 1 first and then lengths on occasions 2? Thank you in advance.

Regards,

Julien

messages.author: 8d0a80872239233d
messages.subject: Re: Area offset in spAbundance
parts:
Hi again,

I just realized I was not using the adequate function. When I switched to msNMix, the software actually asked for a vector of length equal to the number of sites.

Regards,

Julien

messages.author: 0b274a0ee3490d75
messages.subject: Re: Area offset in spAbundance
parts:
Hi Julien,

Glad you were able to figure this out. Yes, the length of the offset should be equal to the number of sites.

As an aside, 3 species is not really enough to fit a regular multi-species model as the default is implemented, since species-level effects are treated as random effects. Thus, with only three species, you only have three levels to estimate a variance parameter, which is not much information. Instead, you could fit a separate model for each species, or if you wanted to fit all together I would suggest setting the tags "independent.betas" and "independent.alphas" = TRUE in the prior list, which will separately estimate species-specific effects. See this thread from the HMecology google group a while back on how to go about doing that and let me know if you have any questions.

Jeff
